local_checks.invariant: Contributor code cannot acquire protected repository, deployment, signing or production credential authority through a workflow event.
local_checks.result: All three workflows use push and/or pull_request, runs-on ubuntu-latest, and explicit contents:read (.github/workflows/security-gate.yml:2-12; algocom.yml:2-11; android-library.yml:2-11). No pull_request_target, workflow_run, external issue trigger, secrets reference, write token declaration, id-token permission, protected environment, publication or deployment sink appears. Security workflow runs checked-out contributor code and docker containers with a trust-authenticated synthetic PostgreSQL service (:13-27); that DB administrator authority is purpose-created test authority, not source evidence of production access. Ephemeral app/demo values are generated and masked at :39-46. Default checkout credential persistence is not overridden, but the source-declared token permission is read-only and no privileged consumer is present; this alone is not a vulnerability. No source-complete escalation candidate was found.

unresolved: Hosted runner isolation, effective repository/organization token policy, fork approval rules, private repository read scope and branch-protection requirements are not locally observed.

No target-controlled workflow/build/scanner was executed: the mandatory complete OS sandbox lacks configured memory, process-count and scratch disk limits. No network/provider/registry request was made.
hardening: Pin action/image identities to reviewed immutable digests for stronger supply-chain reproducibility; mutable tags alone do not establish an exploit.
Consider persist-credentials:false for checkout when later steps do not need Git authentication; no write authority or actual secret disclosure was established.
Require independent branch review of workflow, scanner and allowlist changes; repository branch-protection state is unobserved.
Broaden custom static rules if relying on CI as comprehensive audit coverage; current Semgrep/static checks intentionally cover only narrow JavaScript invariants.
Python requirements pin only jsonschema directly; transitive/hash locking and Gradle dependency verification would strengthen integrity without constituting a demonstrated vulnerability.

Existing instrumentation source covers vault tamper/logout and Room reopen; PublicSync network failure, partial template batch, origin switch and retention lifecycle need future synthetic emulator coverage within a compliant sandbox.
